explain.say: About 1.4 billion people live in India. How can a letter find just one house? With a clever code! Look at the board. We're going to zoom in, from the whole country to one front door, using the PIN code 110001, in New Delhi.

faq.q: What does each digit of a PIN code mean?
faq.a: In India's six-digit PIN code, the first digit is the region, the second the sub-region, the third the sorting district, and the last three the delivery post office.
asks: How does a PIN code work?

faq.q: When did India start using PIN codes?
faq.a: On 15 August 1972. PIN stands for Postal Index Number.
asks: What does PIN code stand for?

faq.a: They let sorting machines and staff find the right area in seconds, without reading the whole address, so millions of letters can be sorted quickly.
asks: What is the point of a postcode?

faq.q: Are postcodes the same in every country?
faq.a: No. India uses six digits, the USA uses five-digit ZIP codes, the UK mixes letters and numbers like SW1A 1AA, and Brazil uses eight-digit CEP codes.

faq.q: Do postcodes help with anything else?
faq.a: Yes. Map apps, delivery companies and emergency services use them to find places quickly.

facts: India introduced the six-digit Postal Index Number system on 15 August 1972.
US ZIP codes, introduced in 1963, have five digits.

quiz.say: In an Indian PIN code, what does the first digit show?
quiz.show: In an Indian PIN code, what does the first digit show?
quiz.why: The first digit stands for one of India's postal regions.

wrong.1: The house number is written separately in the address.
wrong.2: Street names are written in words, not in the PIN code.

quiz.say: How many digits are in an Indian PIN code?
quiz.show: How many digits are in an Indian PIN code?
quiz.why: Indian PIN codes have six digits, like 110001.

wrong.1: Four digits is too few; some other countries use four.
wrong.2: Ten digits is more like a phone number.
